why: The two reds had two different causes, both test-isolation slips in feature 415's own new code, and each was caught by the gate as it is meant to be. Gate 1 (817 failed): a T03 test started the real cover_changed.py, which ran a nested coverage run that overwrote the gate's data. Gate 2 (3 failed): planner tests inherited INCR_NO_CUTOFF=1 from T05's own export. Each fix is narrow and confined to the tests, moves no engine behavior, undoes nothing earlier, and the second red (3 failures) is a strict, explained subset of the first; nothing oscillates and no fixed number is being defended, so this is not packing.

why: This is the second appearance of the first red's cause, not a third cause. The 18:59Z gate (817 failed) and the 19:17Z gate (489 failed) have the same signature, pytest INTERNALERROR 'no such table: context', and the 19:08Z ruling accepted the wrong cause for the first one (a test starting the real cover_changed.py). It could not have seen that, because the bundle lists 20 collateral test names and not the INTERNALERROR line. The new cause has a mechanism the bundle bears out: T03 made land.py run cover_changed.py beside the gate in the same tree with no COVERAGE_FILE of its own, and it landed on the DIRECT route, so the two first met at T05's gated landing. The 19:05Z gate (3 failed, a separate env leak now fixed) did not show the signature, which fits a collision that depends on what cover_changed has to run. Nothing reverses or oscillates, each red narrows the causes, and no fixed number is being defended, so this is not packing. The session fixed this cause before coming back, although the last ruling said to bring a third cause here first. That is waived: it is the first cause correctly diagnosed, not a new one.
asked: a second red make done in a row
what: One more make land for T05, with the COVERAGE_FILE fix in scripts/gates/cover_changed.py. It counts as green only if all of these hold: (1) the gate's pytest output has no INTERNALERROR and no 'no such table' line, and failed_tests is 0; (2) the three planner tests are green by name (test_plan_returns_a_full_run_when_the_projection_is_over_the_fraction, test_e_over_the_fraction_the_PLANNER_runs_everything_and_keeps_the_trees, test_e_a_landing_runs_what_it_reaches_over_the_fraction), since the 19:17Z list is cut to 20 of 489 and cannot show that gate 2's fix held; (3) cover_changed actually ran beside that gate with real work and wrote its data in its own temporary directory, with no stray .coverage* files left in the clone root afterwards. A green gate with cover_changed idle does not prove the fix. The T03 stand-in test can stay: it is harmless and keeps a gate from starting a nested real check. If a fourth gate is red with the sqlite signature, bring it back and it will be ruled process-fault: by then the shared-tree coverage collision is a fault in the landing's design, not a slip.
